ELECTION RESEARCH — 2026 B.C. provincial general election

Background for the roundup's election stories and any race the hosts mention. It is not the deep dive's subject.

**FINDINGS — Cariboo-Chilcotin**

Filed candidates: Kathryn Askew (BC NDP), Lorne Doerkson (Conservative), Douglas Gook (BC Green). Elections BC's candidate report lists all three (elections.bc.ca, candidate website report, Oct. 2026), and BC Ballot and Studio X News carry the same names.

- **Kathryn Askew (BC NDP).** 100 Mile Free Press (Oct. 1, 2026) reports she is a retired school teacher from Canim Lake, named as the NDP candidate. The BC NDP release names her as its Cariboo-Chilcotin candidate (bcndp.ca, undated in my read) and says she has 32 years in education, including leadership roles with the BC Teachers' Federation and her local union. The release also says that in 2025 she was the NDP candidate for Mission—Matsqui—Abbotsford in the federal election. I did not find her vote share in that race. Stephen Taylor's 2025 results page reports Brad Vis (Conservative) won that riding with 56.7% and Jeff Howe (Liberal) placed second with 36.6% (stephentaylor.ca, 2025 results). No controversy involving Askew was found in the sources read.

- **Lorne Doerkson (Conservative).** Sourced background: MLA for Cariboo-Chilcotin since 2020, first elected as a B.C. Liberal, re-elected in 2024 as a B.C. Conservative (Elections BC results, 2024-10-19). BC Ballot gives the 2024 Conservative margin in the riding as 7,722 votes (bcballot.ca, 2026 candidate page). Carried forward from prior research: Elections BC's 2020 statement of votes shows him at 6,600 votes (51.25%) for the Liberals. The Globe and Mail (Sept. 26, 2026) reports he took over as Conservative leader. Wikipedia describes him as interim leader since 2026.
  - *Controversy (campaign, 2026):* Vaughn Palmer's Vancouver Sun column (Oct. 7, 2026) says Doerkson told reporters he had made "no promises at all" on auto insurance, and Palmer argues he had made four. Palmer writes that Doerkson twice denied making commitments of any kind. This is the columnist's assessment, and the outlet's article was paywalled in my read. Doerkson's response is the denial reported in that column.
  - *Related party matter (not about Doerkson personally):* The Tyee (Oct. 8, 2026) reports Doerkson fired the party's Victoria-Beacon Hill candidate after social media posts the BC NDP flagged as racist. CityNews (Oct. 14, 2026) reports a Conservative campaign director under fire over social posts will stay on, Doerkson says.
  - No other controversy involving Doerkson was established in the sources checked.

- **Douglas Gook (BC Green).** Elections BC's candidate report lists him for Cariboo-Chilcotin (2026). The Caledonia Courier (Oct. 2024) reports he had run unsuccessfully as a Green candidate in North Cariboo, now Prince George-Cariboo North, four times, including a 2017 Nechako Lakes bid where he took about nine per cent. My Cariboo Now calls his 2020 bid his fourth time running for the Greens in that riding. Carried forward from prior research: the Elections BC 2020 statement of votes shows him at 707 votes (6.38%) in Cariboo North. The two accounts don't reconcile the count of runs, and the show has not resolved it. CKPG Today (Sept. 13, 2024) announced him as the Green candidate for Nechako Lakes in 2024. His 2024 result in that riding was not established in the sources read. No controversy was established.

**FINDINGS — Prince George-North Cariboo (includes Quesnel)**

Filed candidates: Denice Bardua (BC NDP), Sheldon Clare (Conservative), Randy Thompson (BC Green). The Quesnel Cariboo Observer (Oct. 7, 2026) reports the list was confirmed by Elections BC after nominations closed Oct. 3. CKPG Today (Oct. 3, 2026) and the Prince George Citizen (candidates finalized) list the same three.

- **Denice Bardua (BC NDP).** CKPG Today (Sept. 24, 2024) reports she was announced as the NDP candidate for this riding in 2024. Her campaign site (denicebardua.bcndp.ca) says she has been a Quesnel resident since 1997 and works in education. BCPoliTracker reports she placed second in 2024 with 3,426 votes, or 17.0%, behind the Conservative candidate. Quesnel Cariboo Observer (Oct. 7, 2026) gives 17.03% for 2024. Her 2024 run is the only earlier run established in the sources read. No controversy was established.

- **Sheldon Clare (Conservative, incumbent).** Sourced background: won the riding for the B.C. Conservatives in 2024 (Elections BC results, 2024-10-19). Carried forward from prior research: Quesnel Cariboo Observer (Oct. 7, 2026) reports 11,430 votes, or 56.82%, in 2024. Times Colonist (Jan. 8, 2026, Canadian Press) reports he said he was running for the B.C. Conservative leadership. CFJC Today (Feb. 28, 2026) reports he suspended that bid, citing a leadership application issue where some signatures were not accepted. He said he "takes full responsibility."
  - *Election-finance penalty (finding):* Elections BC's enforcement notice (dated March 30, 2026) and its April 1, 2026 release (reported by CKPG Today, Apr. 1, 2026, and the Quesnel Cariboo Observer, Apr. 3, 2026) say he was fined $1,500 for accepting anonymous contributions for the 2024 election that exceeded the limit by about $4,000. Elections BC said the investigation found no deliberate attempt to circumvent the law. The Prince George Citizen reported the same penalty. I did not find his response to the penalty in the sources read.
  - *Allegation (Sept. 2026):* CKPG Today (Sept. 18, 2026) reports that in a party group chat about municipal elections, Clare wrote "There's a good number that need hanging," responding to a post by a Parksville mayoral candidate. Clare's statement says the remark was made in jest, was not meant as a threat, and he apologized to anyone who took offense (CKPG Today, Sept. 18, 2026; Prince George Citizen update). The Prince George Citizen headlined his apology as a formal apology. The BC NDP wrote on X that Doerkson "had one last chance to drop him. He didn't." That is the NDP's claim, and Doerkson's response to it was not found.
  - *Allegation (undated in snippet):* PressProgress reports residential-school postings attributed to Clare. The article says neither Clare nor the party responded to its requests for comment. The article's date and full text were not confirmed in my read, and the content appears to predate the 2026 campaign.

- **Randy Thompson (BC Green).** BC Greens' candidate page says he ran as the Green candidate in this riding in 2024 and previously served two years on the party's provincial council (bcgreens.ca). Quesnel Cariboo Observer (Oct. 7, 2026) reports he finished fourth in 2024 with just over four per cent. BCPoliTracker gives 866 votes, 4.3%. Prince George Daily News (Oct. 11, 2026) reports the Greens announced him as the candidate. No controversy was established.

The show has not yet established any earlier provincial election run for Kathryn Askew, Denice Bardua or Randy Thompson.

NO RECORD FOUND: none
